status: Original editorial heuristics assembled from cited research and existing pinned skills. This collection has no measured agent-effectiveness results.

operators.name: Invert an outcome into plausible obstacles
operators.recognize: An intended user outcome is stated but its preconditions, interruptions or failure states are unclear.
operators.reject_when: A small, reversible fix already has a complete accepted behavior and a direct test.
operators.mechanism: State the user-observable goal and negate its success condition. Refine plausible causes of failure to observable conditions, then ask which are feasible in the actual environment.
operators.question_template: What would stop {actor} from achieving {goal} even when the normal flow appears to succeed?
contrasting_answers: The obstacle is reachable under the current platform and workflow.
The obstacle is impossible or already handled under the current contract.
operators.decision_consequence: Changes required recovery, constraints, or acceptance checks only for reachable consequential obstacles.
first_sources: Current product contract and end-to-end user journey
Actual operation states and failure traces
operators.disconfirmation: Demonstrate that the suspected obstacle cannot occur or that a real existing path already handles it.
operators.oracle: Reproduce the specific failed user outcome and its recovery at the necessary runtime tier.
operators.stop: Do not enumerate every imaginable failure; retain only plausible obstacles capable of changing the decision.

operators.name: Contrast competing user interpretations
operators.recognize: An interface proposal is described as intuitive, obvious, compact, automatic or easy without specifying user expectations.
operators.reject_when: Only a known typo or fixed design token is changing; no user interaction or meaning changes.
operators.mechanism: Construct two plausible user expectations and trace the action each person believes a visible control will perform. Check novice, frequent-user and assistive-input paths where relevant.
operators.question_template: What does {actor} expect {control} to do, and who would interpret it differently?
contrasting_answers: The control has one discoverable meaning for intended users.
The control is ambiguous or hides a frequent user job.
operators.decision_consequence: Changes naming, placement, defaults, progressive disclosure or confirmation; may require user research.
first_sources: Observed current journey and product decisions
First-hand user complaints, praise and workarounds
operators.disconfirmation: A user task observation or controlled accessible walkthrough contradicts the assumed mental model.
operators.oracle: Real users or credible proxy task sessions correctly predict and complete the operation, including recovery.
operators.stop: Do not invent user preference or claim survey representativeness from screenshots or forum counts.

operators.name: Cross execution, identity and lifecycle boundaries
operators.recognize: A command, identity, permission, file or state can change between approval, execution and observed completion.
operators.reject_when: The action is pure, synchronous and local with no mutable external identity or side effect.
operators.mechanism: Name the boundary, freeze the intended target, and simulate what changes on either side of the boundary before an asynchronous outcome is known.
operators.question_template: Can {resource} change ownership, scope or availability between {before} and {after}?
contrasting_answers: Target and authority remain stable across the boundary.
Target, authority or outcome may drift or become uncertain.
operators.decision_consequence: Changes identity capture, persistence, retry policy, cancellation and reconciliation safeguards.
first_sources: Concrete production call path and dataflow
operators.disconfirmation: Trace a frozen end-to-end identity across the edge, including a timeout-after-commit or process restart when reachable.
operators.oracle: Exactly the authorized target receives the intended operation, without duplicates or lost recovery state.
operators.stop: Do not impose transaction machinery on read-only or proven idempotent operations.

operators.name: Turn design uncertainty into questions, options and criteria
operators.recognize: There are credible competing implementations or UX designs and the choice has material tradeoffs.
operators.reject_when: An established local pattern already meets constraints and alternatives offer no meaningful different outcome.
operators.mechanism: State one decisive question, at least two real options, non-negotiable constraints and discriminating criteria. Name the strongest rival and what could reverse the choice.
operators.question_template: Which of {option_a} and {option_b} better supports {goal} under {constraint}, and what would reverse that ranking?
contrasting_answers: Option A meets the observed criteria better.
Option B satisfies a neglected high-impact criterion or hard constraint.
operators.decision_consequence: Changes architecture or interaction choice and sets the scope of an informative comparison.
first_sources: Observed usability, risk or performance evidence
operators.disconfirmation: The preferred option violates a constraint or a competing option wins a decision-relevant user outcome.
operators.oracle: Test the important differentiating criterion with the same user task and context across options.
operators.stop: Do not expand the design space indefinitely; choose when extra options cannot plausibly alter the decision.

operators.name: Reverse-audit goal, operation, result and recovery relationships
operators.recognize: A conceptual map or feature inventory seems complete, but an important user goal lacks a linked end-to-end journey.
operators.reject_when: A single directly observable path answers the scoped question without disputed relationships.
operators.mechanism: Walk user goal → available action → permission/identity → state transition → visible result → recovery, and reverse-walk each feature back to a legitimate user need.
operators.question_template: Which required relation between {actor}, {goal} and {result} is absent from the current model?
contrasting_answers: A known relation exists in source material but was not modeled.
The relation remains unknown or unsupported after scoped coverage checks.
operators.decision_consequence: Triggers model repair or a qualified investigation, not automatic feature implementation.
first_sources: Existing concept inventory and product source
operators.disconfirmation: Find the alleged missing relation in an unextracted source, synonym, alternate representation or existing implementation.
operators.oracle: State the exact competency question and show the corrected provenance-backed edge or a bounded unresolved gap.
operators.stop: Missing edge in an open-world graph never establishes product absence or novelty.

operators.name: Challenge applicability and transfer of attractive advice
operators.recognize: A widely repeated rule, impressive source or prior solution is about to be applied to a materially different environment.
operators.reject_when: The original contract, platform version and exact use case have already been verified identical.
operators.mechanism: Identify assumptions the source relies on: framework, version, actor, owner, lifecycle, mutability, user goals and evidence tier. Find the nearest counterexample.
operators.question_template: Which hidden precondition of {rule} fails in {environment}?
contrasting_answers: The source's tested preconditions match the host case.
A version, ownership, or authorization difference makes the transfer unsafe.
operators.decision_consequence: Adopt, adapt, narrow or reject the upstream rule with rationale.
first_sources: Host project's actual contract and source
operators.disconfirmation: Demonstrate a concrete host condition that invalidates the source's presumed invariant.
operators.oracle: Verify the adapted mechanism at the actual host boundary; preserve negative transfer evidence.
operators.stop: A popular source or number of copies cannot substitute for checking applicability.

operators.name: Search evidence that would oppose the provisional hypothesis
operators.recognize: A recommendation relies on one type of source, a popular example or an unchallenged claimed absence.
operators.reject_when: The claim is low-stakes and adding a second source could not affect any relevant decision.
operators.mechanism: Search independent source classes, opposite user testimony, alternate-language terminology, working implementations and a genuinely disconfirming case.
operators.question_template: What evidence would make {claim} wrong or inapplicable for {actor}?
contrasting_answers: Independent evidence is compatible with the scoped claim.
Contrary evidence reveals an overlooked user segment, version or prior implementation.
operators.decision_consequence: Reassess confidence, scope, possible user need and prior-art novelty.
first_sources: Independent user testimony in original languages
operators.disconfirmation: Find one credible contradictory implementation, source contract or user task with matching scope.
operators.oracle: Record searched and inaccessible source classes, contradiction and remaining evidence limits.
operators.stop: Stop after a bounded search if more sources cannot alter a consequential decision; non-findings are not proof of nonexistence.

operators.name: Find what could pass a test while still failing the user's goal
operators.recognize: A build, mock, API acknowledgment, screen preview or green CI is used to claim a working feature.
operators.reject_when: The claim is explicitly and narrowly about compilation or a pure isolated function only.
operators.mechanism: List the observed boundary of the existing test. Invent a feasible counterexample where that test passes but the end-to-end user outcome fails.
operators.question_template: How could {evidence} pass while {goal} still fails for {actor}?
contrasting_answers: Current evidence exercises all boundaries needed for the narrow claim.
An unexercised platform, service or UI boundary could still fail.
operators.decision_consequence: Adds an appropriately scoped independent acceptance test or narrows the success claim.
operators.disconfirmation: Show that the exact claimed user-visible outcome already executes inside the verified test boundary.
operators.oracle: Reproduce the requested behavior on the necessary platform and report which boundaries remain untested.
operators.stop: Do not demand physical-device testing to establish a narrow pure-function property.

operators.name: Look for valuable interactions among otherwise complete subsystems
operators.recognize: Two or more independently functioning capabilities share user objects, actors or operations, but the combined journey is absent or awkward.
operators.reject_when: The proposed linkage has no identified user benefit or crosses prohibited authority boundaries.
operators.mechanism: Connect goals and objects across subsystem maps, then hypothesize a joint user task; distinguish known connections, unresearched linkages and genuinely new composition.
operators.question_template: Could a user completing {goal} benefit from linking {system_a} and {system_b}, and which operation owns that relation?
contrasting_answers: A cross-subsystem link enables an observed valuable user journey.
The link is already implemented, unwanted, unsafe or unsupported by evidence.
operators.decision_consequence: Triggers a qualified product opportunity hypothesis, not an automatic requirement.
first_sources: Observed multi-step user workflows and manual workarounds
operators.disconfirmation: Find established prior art or evidence users do not want the linked workflow; prove existing code already handles it.
operators.oracle: Validate user need and task correctness independently before selecting an implementation.
operators.stop: Do not invent features merely to fill sparse graph regions or maximize connectivity.
